reviews.summary: This paper uses GW250114 ringdown measurements to constrain phenomenological modifications of the Teukolsky effective potential. It maps potential-deformation coefficients into changes of the fundamental quasinormal frequency and combines published damped-sinusoid posteriors with mass and spin information from an inspiral–merger–ringdown analysis. A Gaussian likelihood approximation makes the calculation inexpensive. Two prior prescriptions widen the remnant-parameter uncertainty to represent possible departures from the general-relativistic prediction. When varied individually, the tested complex deformation coefficients remain consistent with zero. The contribution is a practical translation from spectral measurements to perturbation-equation parameters. The resulting bounds depend on that prior construction, the single-mode approximation and the treatment of theoretical uncertainty, so they are best viewed as conditional constraints motivating a fuller joint analysis.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly central to Teukolsky deformations, quasinormal modes and observational black-hole perturbation tests.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected analysis defines an explicit likelihood and explores alternative remnant priors using public posteriors. The constraints remain sensitive to simplified uncertainty handling and one-at-a-time deformations rather than a full joint waveform analysis.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, remnant-prior construction, portions of Sec. III and Sec. IV. Only the fundamental mode and individually varied deformations are used. Dependence on GR-informed remnant posteriors and omitted sky-localization uncertainty limit the interpretation. Figures were not visually inspected; inference and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: all beyond-Teukolsky deviation parameters, when varied one at a time, are in agreement with GR.

reviews.summary: This paper considers highly eccentric, bound EMRIs whose orbital periods exceed a detector's observation window, producing isolated pericenter eruptions. An analytic steady-state continuity model estimates their Galactic-center population and rate, while a LISA noise prescription supplies illustrative signal-to-noise values. Under the adopted two-mass population model, the authors predict hundreds to thousands of long-period systems and several to tens of observable eruptions per year. They also use Schwartz-space smoothing to discuss transient Fourier analysis and attenuation when a time-domain taper overlaps an eruption. The contribution connects an early EMRI population to a specific signal-processing issue. Its numerical rates remain model-dependent, and the formal energy-preservation argument requires care when translated into optimal inference with realistic colored noise and finite data.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses eccentric EMRIs, transient gravitational waves and practical analysis of future LISA signals.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text develops a quantitative but explicitly illustrative population model and identifies a clear taper-overlap effect. General claims of estimator optimality would need further detector-level validation beyond signal-energy arguments.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, Sec. 2.5, windowing and smoothing excerpts, and Sec. 10. Rates depend on a steady-state Galactic-center model, sharp relaxation/GW transition and two secondary masses. A flat-top taper covering the eruption is already acknowledged as equivalent on its support. Figures were not visually inspected; population calculations and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Discussion immediately before Sec. 10, flat-top taper qualification
reviews.evidence_quote: If data analysis employs a flat-top window

reviews.summary: This paper proposes that collisions between an EMRI and a warped accretion disk explain correlated brightness and recurrence intervals in quasi-periodic X-ray eruptions. A brightness–recurrence diagram organizes the predicted pattern into an elliptical track driven by orbital precession, whose orientation depends on orbital direction and secondary type. Applied to GSN 069, the model accommodates either a prograde star or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. Simplified post-Newtonian trajectories and Gaussian flares roughly reproduce selected light-curve epochs, although the secular decline in flare amplitude is missed. The contribution is a geometric diagnostic linking disk structure, EMRI motion and electromagnetic observations. A future LISA signal could help distinguish interpretations, but that prospect depends on the black-hole-secondary scenario and uncertain long-term disk-driven evolution.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly connects EMRIs, environmental disk interactions, orbital precession and possible electromagnetic precursors to gravitational-wave observations.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected model is compared with observed timing/brightness patterns and includes a parameter survey. Its light-curve treatment is simplified, and the data retain a secondary-type degeneracy.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, Sec. V, Sec. VII and part of Appendix A. Collisions are treated approximately, disk evolution and individual collision kicks are omitted, and absolute flare fading is not fitted. LISA follow-up is a conditional forecast. Figures were not visually inspected; fits and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: precession and alignment of the warped disk are omitted

reviews.summary: This paper proposes using gravitational-wave polarization as a reference for the intrinsic orientation of a resolved electromagnetic counterpart in a strongly lensed merger. Comparing that reference with each apparent jet axis measures an image's lens-induced orientation offset. The framework combines these offsets with image positions, delays and magnifications, then forecasts performance with mock binary-neutron-star populations and a joint Fisher analysis. Under favorable assumptions, orientation offsets are measurable in up to about one third of selected events. The contribution is an additional local lens diagnostic that is invariant under a mass-sheet transformation. Practical opportunities are restricted because polarization is best measured at inclinations where jets are harder to observe, and real jet–orbit misalignment and counterpart uncertainties reduce the forecast yield.
reviews.relevance_reason: Direct overlap with gravitational-wave lensing, polarization and multimessenger constraints on lens structure.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text specifies the joint framework, includes detection selection and coverage diagnostics, and explicitly tests orientation-error and alignment-scatter effects. It also identifies the mass-sheet degeneracy and observational bottlenecks.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, uncertainty/likelihood discussion, opening of Sec. 3, Sec. 4 excerpts and Sec. 5. Forecasts use Fisher/Gaussian approximations and favorable counterpart information. Static-lens polarization transport and jet–orbit alignment are assumed; realistic EM resolution is restrictive. Figures were not visually inspected; forecasts and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: we neglect non-Gaussian posteriors, angular structure of the lens, and microlensing by stars

reviews.summary: This paper analyzes repeated lensing of continuous gravitational waves from a source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. Lense–Thirring precession periodically brings the orbit close to edge-on, producing a train of short amplified episodes at successive conjunctions. The authors derive orbital, precession, blast and train timescales and examine an illustrative neutron star around Sagittarius A*. Large peak magnification is offset by a small duty cycle, so the integrated detection gain is modest. Detecting the recurring pattern requires an orbital model that preserves coherence despite rapid Doppler modulation. The contribution is a distinctive lensing timing signature tied to frame dragging. Its observational prospects depend on a rare close neutron-star system, its spin and ellipticity, and sufficiently accurate orbital tracking.
reviews.relevance_reason: Direct overlap with gravitational-wave lensing, relativistic orbital precession and compact objects near massive black holes.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text develops analytic timescale and magnification estimates and explicitly discusses Doppler-limited searches, low duty cycle and source scarcity. The detector forecast remains an illustrative scenario requiring careful coherence and statistic modeling.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, opening of Sec. II and Secs. IX–XI. Weak-field precession, geometric-optics lensing and a favorable neutron-star example are assumed. Expected source counts are below unity before further spin/orbit restrictions. Coherent versus semicoherent detection conventions need care. Figures were not visually inspected; forecasts and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. IX, Does lensing boost detectability?
reviews.evidence_quote: the lensing introduces a small correction to the integrated signal-to-noise ratio.

reviews.summary: SPLIT introduces a loosely coherent Bayesian framework for long EMRI and IMRI signals whose phase evolution may be modeled imperfectly. It analyzes shorter coherent blocks with a heavy-tailed likelihood and connects their evolving parameters through a flexible Markovian prior. A GPU implementation uses sequential Gibbs sampling. Vacuum injections agree with coherent baselines, while an accretion-perturbed IMRI example reduces the largest reported parameter bias from about 4.8 to 0.5 standard deviations with five blocks. The contribution is a tunable robustness–precision trade-off for inference before more accurate coherent follow-up. Its enlarged posterior space is costly to sample, and the demonstrated improvement depends on a limited injection set and chosen hyperparameters rather than a comprehensive realistic-LISA validation.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly relevant to EMRI waveform inference and robustness to environmental modeling errors.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text includes coherent control cases, a misspecified environmental injection and block-number comparisons, with explicit bias, precision and runtime trade-offs.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading of this version: abstract, Introduction, portions of Sec. III.4 and Sec. IV. The environmental example fixes primary spin to zero and explores few injections. Hyperparameter sensitivity and non-Gaussian data artifacts need broader validation. Sampling costs substantially exceed the coherent benchmark. Figures were not visually inspected; code and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the chain convergence rate is still significantly slower than in the fully-coherent case.

reviews.summary: This paper studies exceptional points where two scalar quasinormal modes of a Kerr-Sen black hole coalesce, and compares their structure with Kerr-Newman. Instead of scanning the spectrum across parameter space, the authors solve a continued-fraction secular equation together with its frequency derivative, tracing degeneracy lines in spin, charge and scalar mass. The lines remain near extremality and reach the massless-scalar plane; following modes around an endpoint exchanges their labels. A nonrotating WKB comparison and a near-extremal asymptotic expansion provide consistency checks. The contribution is an efficient way to map spectral topology and identify path-dependent mode assignments. Its implications for observable gravitational ringdown remain prospective because the calculations concern test scalar fields rather than coupled gravitational perturbations.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly concerns quasinormal-mode degeneracies, near-extremal black-hole perturbations and resonance-related spectral behavior. The scalar setting limits immediate waveform applications.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text gives an explicit double-root method, tabulated degeneracies, WKB comparisons and an asymptotic check, with supporting notebooks and data identified. These support a substantial technical result within the test-field scope.
reviews.limitations: Selective text inspection: abstract, introduction, Sec. III degeneracy method, portions of Sec. IV numerical checks/results, Sec. V final remarks and Sec. VI data availability. Scalar fields only; higher-spin couplings and observational excitation remain untested here. WKB checks cover a restricted nonrotating limit. No visual figure inspection, notebook execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. IV, comparison of continued-fraction frequencies with sixth-order WKB in the nonrotating massless-scalar limit.
reviews.evidence_quote: For \ell\geq 2 , the results agree to within 10^{-5}

reviews.summary: This study asks when LISA can identify nonzero eccentricity in an EMRI using a computationally cheaper semi-coherent search. FastEMRIWaveforms injections compare eccentric and circular hypotheses, first without noise and then with detector response and calibrated noise thresholds. At fixed total matched-filter SNR 50, eccentricity becomes distinguishable around final eccentricity 0.05, but a single harmonic loses sensitivity above roughly 0.1 as power spreads across harmonics. Multiple harmonics mitigate that loss in noise-free tests; their noisy detection benefit remains uncalibrated. Controlled relaxation and Hills populations illustrate different detectability patterns. These results clarify an important search-design trade-off, but their fixed Schwarzschild systems, orientations and tightly restricted eccentricity-search parameters prevent interpretation as realistic population rates or blind-search forecasts.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses EMRI gravitational-wave searches, eccentricity and LISA selection effects, with practical consequences for waveform harmonics and astrophysical interpretation.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected methods and results separate noise-free harmonic tests from noisy single-harmonic forecasts, calibrate false-alarm thresholds and acknowledge optimizer limitations. The controlled injection study offers substantial evidence, though its parameter restrictions limit generalization.
reviews.limitations: Selective text inspection: abstract/introduction, Sec. II.5 analysis setup, portions of Sec. III.3 source/eccentricity detection, Sec. IV conclusions and software statement. Fixed masses, zero spin, orientation and SNR; eccentricity searches use bounds within 1% of injected parameters. Multi-harmonic noisy gains are untested. No figure inspection, code execution or derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. III.3.2 Detection of eccentricity, discussing intrinsic-parameter bounds.
reviews.evidence_quote: The use of these narrower bounds represents an important limitation of our analysis.

reviews.summary: The authors extend relativistic perturbation theory for a spherical black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter with nonzero radial pressure. A polytropic generalization of the Einstein cluster supplies analytic backgrounds, while strictly static and irrotational prescriptions close the axial perturbation equations. Geodesic and axial quasinormal-mode corrections are dominated by an environmental redshift enhanced by radial pressure, with sixth-order WKB results supporting the leading analytic scaling. Magnetic tidal Love numbers respond more strongly in relative terms and can change sign under one prescription, although their normalization and interpretation require care. The framework helps organize environmental effects relevant to ringdown and future inspiral modeling. It remains an effective-fluid model with inner-region energy-condition violations, closure dependence and no completed polar-sector phenomenology.
reviews.relevance_reason: Combines environmental effects, black-hole perturbation theory, quasinormal modes and tidal response, closely matching several core interests. It supplies a framework rather than an EMRI waveform calculation.
reviews.quality_reason: Explicit backgrounds, leading analytic scalings, WKB comparisons and documented closure alternatives provide substantial technical support. Restricted spectral checks, effective-fluid validity and prescription-dependent tidal interpretation temper broader physical claims.
reviews.limitations: Selective text inspection: abstract/introduction, opening Sec. II, Sec. III energy-condition discussion, Secs. IV.2–IV.3 and most of Sec. V discussion. Spherical backgrounds and axial results; inner-region dominant-energy violations, closure choices and Love-number normalization remain material caveats. No visual figure inspection, notebook execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. IV.3 Tidal Love numbers, before the magnetic Love-number formulas.
reviews.evidence_quote: the definition and normalization of magnetic Love numbers in environmental spacetimes are subtle and prescription dependent.

reviews.summary: This paper proposes modified Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz equations for damping and oscillation frequencies in thermal integrable quantum field theories. Holographic relations between thermal correlators and black-hole quasinormal modes motivate an unusual analytic continuation, while selected secular terms in form-factor expansions determine driving terms. The construction reproduces an exact Ising damping result and the leading low-temperature expansion. For the interacting E8 theory, predicted complex frequencies enter a fit to tensor-network simulations, with eleven complex amplitudes adjusted. This offers a potentially efficient route around difficult real-time resummations, but all-order equivalence, the full mode spectrum and generalized-hydrodynamic extensions remain conjectural. Its connection to the digest is primarily conceptual: these thermal-field-theory modes do not directly supply astrophysical black-hole ringdown or EMRI predictions.
reviews.relevance_reason: Shares quasinormal-mode and holographic spectral concepts, but studies thermalization in integrable QFT rather than astrophysical perturbations, gravitational-wave signals or EMRIs.
reviews.quality_reason: Exact-limit recovery, a leading thermal-order check and an independent tensor-network comparison support the proposal. General resummation equivalence remains conjectural, and the illustrated E8 comparison fits many amplitudes at one temperature over a finite time window.
reviews.limitations: Selective text inspection: abstract/introduction, spectral motivation, portions of the QNM-TBA/form-factor construction, numerical comparison, conjectures/discussion and supplemental E8 simulation/fit details. No all-order proof or full-spectrum result. The inspected fit uses eleven complex amplitudes. No visual figure inspection, simulation execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Some additional conjectures, discussing the scope of the proposed QNM TBA.
reviews.evidence_quote: it is clear that it does not yet predict the full QNM spectrum.
